## Minneapolis bar-service catering shortlist

| Business | City | Why it fits a holiday party |
|---|---|---|
| **Surdyk’s Catering** | Minneapolis | Comprehensive bar service with expert-selected wine, beer and spirits, plus Sidebar signature cocktails. |
| **Steady Pour** | Minneapolis | Dedicated off-site bartending/bar caterer; holds an Alcohol Caterer’s Permit and offers hosted, partial-hosted, cash-bar, and (for some events) client-provided-alcohol formats. |
| **Mintahoe Catering & Events** | Minneapolis | Full beverage catering: top-shelf liquor, extensive wine, beer, bartenders, setup/cleanup, glassware upgrades, and cocktail/mocktail add-ons. |
| **Create Catering & The Dining Studio** | Minneapolis | Standard and premium full-bar packages, selected wine and craft beer, custom craft cocktails, and bartenders. |
| **Sterling Catering** | Minneapolis | Full bar service with domestic/imported beer, premium liquor, extensive wine list, and professional bartenders/servers; says it is licensed and insured. |

**Yes—Surdyk’s is on the list, and it looks particularly full-service.** Beyond bar service, it offers antipasti stations, hors d’oeuvres, buffet dinners, and support with **menu planning, staffing, and rentals**. Its bar offering includes selected wine, beer and spirits and signature cocktails from Sidebar at Surdyk’s—so it is a strong fit if you want one vendor to manage food *and* beverage logistics rather than bartending alone.

Sources: [Surdyk’s full-service page](https://www.surdykscatering.com/full-service-catering) · [Steady Pour](https://www.steadypour.com/bar-catering) · [Mintahoe](https://www.mintahoe.com/catering/bar-beverage-service/) · [Create](https://www.createcaters.com/beverage-service-menu/) · [Sterling](https://www.sterlingcateringmn.com/)

## Practical Instant Pot mulligatawny soup (nonalcoholic)
Adapted from [Simply Happy Foodie’s Instant Pot Mulligatawny](https://www.simplyhappyfoodie.com/instant-pot-mulligatawny-soup/). It contains no alcohol; use vegetable broth and coconut milk for a vegetarian version.

**Ingredients (4–6 servings)**
- 2 Tbsp olive oil; 4 Tbsp butter (or extra oil)
- 1 diced onion, 3 diced celery stalks, 2 diced carrots, ½ diced green bell pepper
- 3 minced garlic cloves; 2 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1½ Tbsp curry powder; 1½ tsp garam masala; ¼ tsp each nutmeg, cinnamon, dried thyme, black pepper; ½ tsp salt
- 6 cups low-sodium vegetable broth (or chicken broth)
- 1 drained 15-oz can diced tomatoes; ½ cup rinsed white rice; 1 diced apple; 3 whole cloves
- 1 cup coconut milk (or heavy cream) mixed with ¼ cup flour
- Optional: 1 lb cubed chicken breast (omit for vegetarian)

**Basic method**
1. Use **Sauté**: brown the optional chicken briefly and remove. Sauté butter/oil with the onion, celery, carrots, and pepper until soft; add garlic and ginger for 1 minute. Stir in spices.
2. Add broth, scraping up any browned bits. Add chicken (if using), tomatoes, rice, apple, and cloves.
3. Seal and pressure-cook on **High for 7 minutes**. Naturally release for **20 minutes**, then release remaining pressure.
4. Switch back to Sauté. Stir in the flour-coconut-milk mixture and simmer just until thickened. Taste and adjust salt; serve hot with naan or crusty bread.
